title: 722 NGOs had registration cancelled in 15 years, minister tells Parliament
excerpt: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed listed late renewals, forged letters of intent and misused grants as reasons, and said the government would stay strict.

image.alt: The NGO Affairs Bureau building in Dhaka, which registers and oversees NGOs receiving foreign funds
image.credit: Wasiul Bahar / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
The registrations of 722 NGOs were cancelled and their work shut down between 2009 and 2024, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told Parliament on Monday, 9 November, NTV Online and Kaler Kantho reported. Salahuddin Ahmed, who is also the minister in charge of the Prime Minister’s Office, oversees the NGO Affairs Bureau. He was answering a question from Advocate Md Jalal Uddin, the ruling party MP for Kishoreganj-2.

Why registrations were cancelled

The minister gave four reasons, according to NTV:

  • Failing to apply for renewal of registration on time.
  • Embezzling grant money, including through forged signatures.
  • Breaking registration conditions or later directives from the NGO Affairs Bureau.
  • Submitting fake letters of intent (LOIs) from donors.

The organisations were blacklisted. The minister did not give a breakdown by reason or by year, or say how many NGOs are registered now. He said the government would keep a strict stance against NGOs involved in illegal activity (Devlens translation from Bangla).

Why it matters

The figure covers 15 years, so it is about 48 a year on average, and it includes NGOs closed only because they missed renewal deadlines. Small organisations are most at risk from that. Under the Foreign Donations (Voluntary Activities) Regulation Act 2016, registration must be renewed every 10 years, and Devlens’s FDVA guide sets out the timelines. Donors and INGOs working through local partners may want to check partners’ registration and renewal dates, and NGOs should keep donor LOIs and fund-release records in order.

What to watch

  • Whether the NGO Affairs Bureau publishes the list of cancelled NGOs and the reasons for each.
  • Any new rules on renewal or foreign funding under the current government.
